senses.sense_definition: Relating to or denoting a style of European architecture, music, and art of the 17th and 18th centuries characterized by ornate detail.

examples.text: The palace is famous for its magnificent <w>baroque</w> architecture and gilded ceilings.
She enjoys listening to <w>baroque</w> music while working in the library.

senses.sense_definition: Highly ornate, elaborate, or extravagant in style.

examples.text: The ballroom was filled with gilded mirrors and <w>baroque</w> decorations.
He designed a <w>baroque</w> frame to display the historic oil painting.

senses.sense_definition: Excessively complicated, convoluted, or elaborate in an impractical way.

examples.text: The company created a <w>baroque</w> bookkeeping system to conceal its financial losses.
Citizens often struggle with the <w>baroque</w> rules of local planning regulations.

senses.sense_definition: A major period and artistic movement in European culture from roughly 1600 to 1750, distinguished by drama, tension, and intricate ornamentation.

examples.text: Many of Rome's most striking fountains were constructed during the <w>Baroque</w>.
Art historians study the transition from the Renaissance into the <w>Baroque</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A chess variant where pieces share common moves but capture opponent pieces through different unique mechanisms.

examples.text: They spent the afternoon learning the unusual rules of <w>Baroque</w>.
A match of <w>Baroque</w> requires very different tactics than standard chess.

senses.sense_definition: An ornate, intricately detailed artistic style or design.

examples.text: The cathedral exterior exhibits an impressive example of late French <w>baroque</w>.
Her jewelry collection is distinguished by an extravagant, heavy <w>baroque</w>.
